response.rationale: Indonesian commonly uses “sepatu bot,” while Malaysian Malay commonly uses “but” for boots. Both denote sturdy footwear covering the ankle.
response.risk_rationale: Malaysian usage may also use the fuller phrase “kasut but” when explicitly referring to footwear.
response.shared_synonym_rationale: “Sepatu bot” is understandable in Malaysia but is not the usual concise Malaysian form; “but” is the ordinary Malaysian preference.
